denominator_rule: Every tool the deep-dive concluded BLOCKED, partitioned into root-cause problems. The partition is MECE and was verified by script: 65 assigned, 65 distinct, 0 missing, 0 duplicated. A problem is never merged, split, reordered or dropped for cost. If a re-run moves a tool to a different problem, it moves — the total never shrinks except by a tool reaching proven.
ordering_rule: sort by (a) tools in the cluster whose MEASURED outcome was a FALSE STATEMENT REACHING THE AUTHOR, desc; then (b) tools the problem blocks, desc; then (c) problem id, asc. Computed, never typed. A tool that cannot be measured costs the loop time; a tool that lies to the author costs the author their work. NOTE: tie-break (c) is a STRING sort, so P10 and P11 precede P9 among the one-tool problems. The cycle numbers in this file are OUTPUT of the rule, recomputed by scripts/toolloop/problem_remaining.py — they are never hand-typed, and the first version of this file had them wrong because I typed them.
cleared_definition: A problem is CLEARED when all four hold. (1) Its invariant is NAMED. (2) The invariant is enforced at ONE chokepoint, with a falsifier proven RED on an ORIGINAL instance and the full suite green. (3) EVERY tool in the cluster has been re-run LIVE at K>=5 and now reads proven, or reads blocked on a DIFFERENT, NAMED cause — which moves it to another problem and is recorded as such. (4) The write-up states what the fix does NOT cover.

spend_policy.decision: OWNER, 2026-08-22: a confirm card for a DESTRUCTIVE or COST-BEARING tool MAY be approved when the target was created by the run's own throwaway fixture and is torn down after. Never against the dogfood book, never against a pre-existing object.
spend_policy.bound: Paid arms run at K=5 like every other arm — the LIVE bar is a distribution, and a cheaper K would be a narrowed denominator wearing a cost excuse. What is bounded is WASTE: the cheapest configured model, the smallest legitimate unit of work, and a card approved at most ONCE per tool per cycle — the second approval proves idempotency and is the only repeat. Every approved paid card records the model, the unit and the observed cost in its ledger row.
spend_policy.why_recorded_here: This REVERSES a standing safety rule from the predecessor loop — 'a card for a COST-BEARING or IRREVERSIBLE tool is NEVER approved'. It is written down so no later session re-derives the old rule from the old GOAL and silently re-blocks ten tools.

problems.third_fix_attempt_2026_08_23:
THE CORRECTION MOVED FROM THE DECLARATION TO THE RESULT, because two declaration fixes were measured and refuted and a third would have been the same move.

  telling settings_provider_inventory what it IS    0/5 -> 1/5 called
  telling settings_list_models what it is NOT       1/5 -> 0/5, and 5 of 5 replies still said
                                                    'what your configured providers currently offer'

The second is the tell: that description states IN CAPITALS that it is not live inventory and names the right tool, and the model read all of it and made the false claim five times out of five. A model reads a DESCRIPTION when it chooses a tool and reads the RESULT when it composes the answer — and the false statement is made at composition time, about data already in hand.

So settings_list_models now returns a `note` on every call saying the list is what is REGISTERED, that a retired model still appears in it, and that 'what does my provider offer' belongs to settings_provider_inventory. A different MECHANISM rather than a louder version of the same one, which is the only justification for a third attempt.

DEPLOYING IT BROKE THE OUTPUT CONTRACT FIRST, and the check caught it: adding a field to the Go struct made the tool return `note` while ai-gateway still served the OLD output schema (additionalProperties:false, models only), so the MCP client REJECTED the whole response — 'Additional properties are not allowed'. A payload change is a contract change on BOTH edges. Re-federated and verified live before measuring anything.
problems.third_fix_attempt_result_2026_08_23:
THE RESULT-LEVEL NOTE WORKED FOR THE ANSWER AND DID NOTHING FOR THE SURFACING, and those turn out to be separable.

  'presented as what the provider currently offers'   pre-fix 9/10   post-fix 0/5
  'registered in your account' (the true statement)    pre-fix 0/10   post-fix 5/5
  settings_provider_inventory actually called          pre-fix 1/10   post-fix 0/5

So the model no longer says the false thing. It says the true thing and then OFFERS to check the live inventory — on a prompt that already asked it to ('Show me what my configured provider actually offers'). The defect that made the answer WRONG is closed; the defect that keeps the tool UNCHOSEN is not, and it was never the same defect.

🔴 AND THE FIX BROKE ITS OWN GATE. answer_expect was none_of:['currently offer'], calibrated on the broken population where that phrase only ever appeared as the false claim. It went RED on 4 of the 5 CORRECT post-fix replies, because the corrected sentence has to name the thing it is not in order to disclaim it: 'These are the models currently REGISTERED in your account. If you want the live inventory of what your providers are currently offering, let me know.' A phrase-level gate calibrated on the broken population marks the very distinction the fix introduces. Replaced with all_of:['registered in your account'] and the separation measured over BOTH populations before adoption (0/10 pre, 5/5 post) — never the other way round.

IT DOES NOT REACH A TOOL WHOSE REFUSAL NAMES NOTHING. The arming keys off catalogue names in the refusal text. 105 of 467 required arguments across the catalogue carry an EMPTY description (75 id-shaped), and for those the refusal falls to its 'does not declare which side supplies them' arm and names no tool by construction. IT DOES NOT STOP THE RETRY STORM. world_delete retried world_get 4-13 times and world_map_create retried 11-13 times BEFORE breaking out to the supplier. IT CANNOT HELP glossary_entity_restore. No supplier exists: a soft-deleted entity is invisible to glossary search, chapter text and project memory, so there is nothing to name and nothing to arm. D-RESTORE-WITH-NO-WAY-TO-SEE-WHAT-IS-RESTORABLE — 10 restore tools ship and only 4 of the things they restore can be listed.

IT DOES NOT ADDRESS THE HOT-SEED STARVATION ITSELF. Three composition suppliers are cut by HOT_SEED_TOKEN_BUDGET (900/356/223 tokens against 2000, 120 candidates keeping 21). The arming is REACTIVE — it rescues them only once the tool has been called and refused. A first turn that needs the supplier before any refusal still cannot see it, and ALWAYS_HOT_READS was deliberately not widened: its own docstring says every addition spends the authoring surface's prefix and to revisit with evidence rather than intuition.
THE ARMING IS CAPPED AT 3 AND RANKS BY NAME LENGTH. A refusal naming four or more catalogue tools arms only three of them, chosen by a rule that has nothing to do with which one unblocks the call.
